meta.note: Content specifications for content-controlled generation. The model is told WHAT to say and chooses every word; the facts are the grading checklist. Novel everyday content, so a memorised passage cannot satisfy it.

specs.scenario: A woman misses her morning bus. She walks to work in the rain. When she arrives, the office is closed.
facts: The office was closed when she arrived.

specs.scenario: An old man buys fish at the market. The price has doubled since last year. He buys less than he planned and walks home.
facts: The price had doubled since last year.
He bought less than he intended.

specs.scenario: A child finds a lost dog near a river. The child brings it home. The parents say it may stay one night.
facts: The child took the dog home.
The parents allowed it to stay for one night.

specs.scenario: A storm damages the roof of a house at night. In the morning a neighbour brings a ladder and helps with the repair. They finish before noon.
A student writes a letter to her brother. She posts it on the way to the station, then discovers her train is two hours late.
facts: The letter was for her brother.
She posted it on the way to a station.
